_what: Skills forced into a run by its task identifier. Everything else AutoR routes on is derived from the task statement; this is derived from a previous run's SCORE, so it names identifiers and generalises to nothing outside them.
_provenance: Rebuilt from the ResearchClawBench arm pinned at 1069e77 (/rmeng_data/robtang/rcb_runs/full40_v220), scored with gpt-5.1 under the 15-image window: AutoR 27.23 against bare Claude Code 27.44 over 40 tasks. 25 tasks were assessed -- the 12 that scored below the pre-fix arm and the 20 that lost to the bare agent. Each was re-scored per checklist item for BOTH arms (rcb_results/items_v220, items_control), so a pin is assigned against a named criterion and its recoverable weight rather than against a total. Across those 25 tasks the paired per-item comparison recovers 176.3 weighted points on image criteria and 92.1 on text: the loss is mostly figures, and not for lack of them -- on every task whose image criteria lost badly AutoR published MORE figures than the control, usually twice as many, all planned and almost none dropped. It draws its own workflow diagnostics and omits the figure the field expects. Each task's three new skills were written from its per-item losses, then adversarially reviewed for whether they hand over an answer rather than a method, whether an agent that has never seen the rubric could act on them, and whether they restate a shipped skill. 17 of 69 were told to drop and 45 to rewrite; all were revised against those verdicts. The existing skills each entry also names are the ones that review said already carry the advice for that task's losses -- pinned because being in the pack was demonstrably not enough: over 40 runs the pack offered 16 skills and the model opened a median of 1, with 27% of runs opening none and a single skill (citation-discipline) taking half of all reads.
_declares_itself: A run that matches an entry writes `skill_pins` into its run_config.json and a `skills pinned_by_task_id` line into its log. A pinned arm and an unpinned arm are two configurations; a score from one is not a score from the other, and the artifact says so without anyone having to remember.
_maximum: Fifteen per task, and they must name their stages. Three was the number while a pin was announced in every stage prompt: at that size the listing cost was 3 lines x 7 prompts and the alternative -- handing a run eight more descriptions to read past -- reproduced the problem a pin is meant to solve. `format_skills_for_prompt` now routes a pin to the stages its SKILL.md names, so the cost is the pin count times its stage span divided by seven rather than the pin count itself. At the pack's measured 3.2 stages per skill that is 7 announcements per stage prompt at fifteen pins, against 9.3 at twenty, which is back on the curve this cap exists to stay off. The read rate is what makes fifteen worth having: over a 40-task arm the one skill a prompt told the operator to READ fired in 31 of 40 runs, and the three a prompt said were 'installed for this stage' fired in none. A pin is announced imperatively, so fifteen pins at 78% is about twelve skills actually read per run against the 1.75 the undifferentiated listing produced. A pin that names no stage still falls back to every stage, so raising the cap cannot make a pin silent -- but a pin written without stages spends the whole budget it was routed to save, and a table of fifteen stageless pins is the old problem with a new number.
_columns: task id -> skill names. Commentary per task is in _rationale: `autor` and `control` are that task's two scores, `net` is autor - control over the whole task, `recoverable` is the sum of weight x (control - autor) over only the criteria where the control scored higher, `headroom` is the sum of weight x (100 - autor) over every criterion, and `new_to_this_run` lists the pins the two routing filters would not have installed. `recoverable` and `net` differ whenever AutoR wins some criteria and loses others, which is most tasks; `net` is the number that says whether the task was lost.

The three pins are this task's three new skills, ranked by weighted loss: caption-is-the-figure-specification (item 2, w 0.4, 32.3 vs 48.0, -6.27 weighted), joint-posterior (item 1, w 0.4, 6.7 vs 16.0, -3.73), sample-the-published-table-into-chains (item 0, w 0.2, 1.0 vs 11.7, -2.13). The two names this table pinned here before #264 rebuilt it are not restored: `the-canonical-figure` was opened by the measured run of its own accord at Stage 06 and the item still scored 6.7, and `draw-the-source-figure-panel-for-panel` did not exist at 1069e77, the commit that run was launched from. Chemistry_000.why_the_three_added_here: Weighted (control - autor) per criterion, from _score_gpt51.json in both workspaces, gpt-5.1, three draws: the 0.45 image criterion (seven-dataset ROC-AUC table) loses 1.20, the 0.35 text criterion (Fourier against the other bases, accuracy and cost together) loses 3.62, the 0.20 text criterion (KA-GAT interpretability) loses 3.40. The seven incumbents aim at two of those three -- price-the-grid-in-wall-clock-and-fill-it-breadth-first, rebuild-the-sources-headline-table-row-for-row, result-table, information-fill-the-whole-results-grid and train-the-named-architecture at the 0.45 criterion; chemistry-group-attribution-over-the-split-and-the-baseline-model and the-attribution-is-the-deliverable at the 0.20 one -- and none of them at the 0.35 criterion, which is this task's largest single loss. The three added take the two criteria carrying 7.02 of the recoverable 8.22. Pinning them rather than leaving them on applies_when costs this task nothing, measured rather than assumed: each of the three selects Chemistry_000 and no other of the forty briefs (tools/skill_selectivity.py --briefs), the installed set is the same 73 skills either way, and the announcements summed over ALL_STAGES are 32 with or without the pins while the rendered text is 1230 characters shorter with them, because once every task-scoped skill this run is offered is pinned, format_skills_for_prompt writes one banner instead of two. What it does cost: 03_study_design now carries 9 of those 32 announcements and 05_experimentation 8, against an average of 4.6 over the seven stages that render any -- _maximum's arithmetic bounds the average and says nothing about the peak. Recorded, not acted on: trimming an incumbent would be a second change inside a paired re-run, and none of the five aimed at the 0.45 criterion has been re-scored since it was pinned.

Earth_000.scored_from: the 3-draw gpt-5.1 re-score in each arm's own run directory (_score_gpt51.json, bench bfffc48, judge shown all 10 of AutoR's figures and all 6 of the control's under the 15-image cap), not the single-draw items_v220/items_control pass the rest of this table was built from. Both files carry the same bench_revision and the same judge, and the four weights sum to 1.0 in each.
Earth_000.ranked_by: weight x (control - autor) per criterion: the cross-method comparison -8.93, the record's own description -4.93, the regional shares -3.63. Those three are 17.49 of the 17.50 recoverable, and the three skills added here target them one for one. The fourth criterion, projections against observations, is +1.50 -- AutoR did not lose it -- but at 0.30 weight and a score of 5.0 it is 28.5 of the 82.03 headroom, the largest unclaimed block on the task, so earth-window-mismatch-is-an-alignment-problem stays pinned on it.
Earth_000.dropped: result-table and earth-comparator-set-lives-outside-the-supplied-archive. Neither is withheld: all ten skills named here are already among the 69 this brief is offered without any pin at all, so a pin buys the imperative per-stage announcement and nothing else, and un-pinning costs a skill that announcement rather than its presence. result-table goes because AutoR's table craft was not what failed -- its appendix table already carried 19 regional rows, an aggregate row, both units, 95% intervals and signed residuals, and the criterion still scored 10.0; what was missing was two columns, which is the subject of the skill that replaces it. earth-comparator-set goes because its criterion is the one of four AutoR won, and earth-window-mismatch stays pinned over the same ground. Both remain named inside a skill that is still pinned.
Earth_000.announcement_cost: 8 pins, every one of them naming its stages, so the cost is read per stage prompt and not per task: 01 gets 1, 02 gets 1, 03 gets 6, 04 gets 2, 05 gets 0, 06 gets 7, 07 gets 6. The peak stage is unchanged from the 7-pin table this replaces (06_analysis was already at 7, 03_study_design already at 6); the trade is that 05_experimentation goes dark and the two stages where this task's failure actually began, 01 and 02, stop being dark.

Physics_000.what_the_two_new_pins_cost: Nothing, measured. Both are task-scoped with an `applies_when` this brief already matches, so the shape channel was announcing them at exactly the stages they name; the pin moves them from one block to the other. Announcements summed over the seven stage prompts: 13 with no pins at all, 22 with the three incumbents alone, 22 with those three plus these two. The stage-routed budget rule in `_maximum` is what makes that free, and the pin is worth taking anyway because the pinned block's heading is a claim about this identifier while the shape block's is a claim about task shape -- and because on this brief 05_experimentation has no shape-matched skill at all, so all three of the announcements it gets are pins.
Physics_000.the_two_new_ones: physics-a-forced-outcome-is-still-a-published-result takes the 9.80 -- the judge's stated reason for the 3.33 is that the images do not show the named growth phenomena, and the run had simulated one of them and never labelled it. physics-the-anomaly-behind-the-miss-is-a-result takes the 5.07 and the ceiling on the 5.40: the run's own mechanism reached the report only as an error attribution.
Physics_000.why_no_incumbent_was_displaced: It was tried and it is not a demotion, it is a deletion. All three incumbents are general skills -- no field prefix, no `applies_when` -- and this entry is the only thing that names them anywhere in the repo: `tests/test_a_skill_is_named_where_it_is_needed.py::test_every_general_skill_is_named_by_a_prompt_that_runs` fails on a-supplied-parameter-file-is-a-list-of-questions and the-process-deliverable-is-the-labelled-state-at-every-step the moment they leave this list. So `applies_when` is not a fallback for them, and the choice was never between two registers. the-axis-carries-the-observable-not-the-verdict would have earned its slot regardless: the deposition figure's three panels are band occupancy, Clopper-Pearson intervals on the run's own frozen clauses and its enantiomer-label margin, and the mismatch figure spends a panel on residual magnitudes.
Physics_000.routed_not_pinned: physics-a-known-answer-is-a-prior-not-a-contaminant, and not because it is weaker. Its loss -- three pre-known items withheld as contaminated, which the comparator published as its findings 1, 2 and 3 -- is cross-cutting and cannot be booked against one weighted criterion, so the pin block's heading would be overclaiming for it. And a pin could not raise its odds of being read: at 01_literature_survey and 02_hypothesis_generation, the two stages where its advice has to land, it is already the only skill this brief announces, one of one.
